examples.en: I am sleepy, so my vision keeps going hazy.
The lighthouse light is faintly flickering in the distance.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 기억이 가물거려서 확실히 말을 못 하겠어요.
examples.en: My childhood memories are hazy, so I cannot say for sure.
The candle flickered in the wind and then went out.
Grandpa says his memory is getting hazy these days.
The street lamps look dim and flickering in the fog.

explain: 불빛이 꺼질 듯 말 듯하거나 기억, 시야가 흐릿해질 때 써요. '깜빡거리다'가 빠르게 켜졌다 꺼지는 느낌이라면, 이 말은 희미해져 가는 느낌이 강해요. 사람이 주어이면 '정신이 가물거리다'처럼 의식이 흐려진다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a light seems about to go out, or when memory or vision grows blurry. '깜빡거리다' feels like quickly turning on and off, while this word feels more like fading away. It can also describe a fading mind, as in '정신이 가물거리다'.

examples.en: Snowfall is expected in the central region tomorrow.
All flights were cancelled because of the snowfall.
The roads froze from the snow, and there were many accidents.
The sudden snowfall paralyzed the morning commute.
This winter's first snowfall came at the end of November.

examples.ko: 시에서는 강설을 대비해 제설 작업을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The city began snow-clearing work in preparation for snowfall.

explain: 일상에서는 '눈이 오다'라고 말하고, '강설'은 일기 예보나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 비가 내리는 '강우'와 짝으로 같이 말하기도 해요. 눈이 오는 양은 보통 '적설량'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '눈이 오다'; '강설' is mostly heard in weather forecasts and news. It pairs with '강우' (rainfall). The depth of accumulated snow is usually called '적설량'.

examples.en: In midwinter the river freezes over completely.
Ice fishing starts only after the lake has frozen.
The temperature dropped overnight and the road froze.
The temperature at which water freezes is zero degrees.

examples.ko: 항구가 결빙하면 배가 다닐 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the port freezes over, ships cannot run.
As the weather warms up, the pond that had frozen is melting.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '얼다', '얼어붙다'를 많이 쓰고, '결빙하다'는 딱딱한 글이나 설명에서 나와요. 도로 안내의 '결빙 구간'처럼 명사로 더 자주 보이고, 반대말은 '해빙'이에요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people say '얼다' or '얼어붙다', while '결빙하다' appears in formal writing and explanations. It is seen more often as a noun, as in '결빙 구간' (icy section) on road notices, and the opposite is '해빙'.

examples.ko: 여름에 음식을 오래 두면 구더기가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you leave food out for long in summer, maggots appear.
I was shocked to see maggots in the trash can.
There was a terrible smell because of the maggots.
Maggots are the larvae of flies.

examples.ko: 이제 구더기도 없고 냄새도 안 나서 다행이에요.
examples.en: Thankfully, there are no maggots and no smell anymore.
My friend ran away, scared by the maggots.

explain: 파리의 애벌레로, 음식물 쓰레기나 상한 음식에 생겨서 징그러운 느낌이 강해요. 속담 '구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까'에도 나와서 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 조금 힘들 수 있어도 해야 할 일은 해야지, 구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까요?
phrases.en: It might be a bit hard, but we have to do what needs doing; we can't stop just because of a little trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방해가 될 일이 있다고 해서 꼭 필요한 일을 포기하면 안 된다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning you shouldn't give up something necessary just because of possible trouble.
phrases.en_equiv: You can't make an omelette without breaking eggs.

explain_en: These are fly larvae that appear in food waste or spoiled food, and the word feels disgusting. It also appears in the proverb '구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까', which is worth knowing.

examples.ko: 강원도 산간 지역에 대설 특보가 발효됐어요.
examples.en: A heavy snow warning has been issued for the mountainous areas of Gangwon Province.
The expressway was closed because of the heavy snow.

examples.ko: 올해 첫 대설로 출근길이 많이 막혔어요.
examples.en: The first heavy snow of the year caused heavy traffic on the morning commute.
Heavy snow is expected tomorrow, so leave early.
After a heavy snowfall, the roads freeze and get slippery.
Daeseol, one of the 24 solar terms, falls around early December.

explain: 눈이 많이 내리는 것을 말하고, 24절기 중 하나의 이름이기도 해요. 일기예보에서는 '대설주의보', '대설경보'처럼 자주 보여요. 갑자기 쏟아지는 눈은 '폭설'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means a large amount of snowfall, and it is also the name of one of the 24 solar terms. In weather forecasts you see it in '대설주의보' and '대설경보'. A sudden heavy snowfall is also called '폭설'.

examples.en: The sky flashed and then there was a loud thunderclap.
Every time the lightning flashed, the child was startled.
The camera flash went off and dazzled my eyes.
I closed my eyes at the sudden flash of light.
After it flashed outside the window, the power went out.

examples.ko: 손전등이 한 번 번쩍한 뒤에 꺼졌어요.
examples.en: The flashlight flashed once and then went out.

explain: 큰 빛이 한 번 잠깐 나타났다 사라질 때 써요. 번개나 카메라 플래시가 대표적이에요. 빛이 계속 반짝이는 것은 '번쩍거리다', '반짝이다'가 더 자연스러워요. 소리와 모양이 비슷한 '번쩍 들다'의 '번쩍'은 빠르게 들어 올리는 모습을 나타내는 부사예요.

phrases.en: snap awake; come to one's senses
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸리거나 멍하던 머리가 갑자기 또렷해질 때 써요. 충격을 받아 현실을 깨달을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sleepy or dazed mind suddenly becomes sharp, or when a shock makes you realize reality.

explain_en: It is used when a big light appears for just a moment and disappears, like lightning or a camera flash. For light that keeps sparkling, '번쩍거리다' or '반짝이다' is more natural. The '번쩍' in '번쩍 들다' is a separate adverb describing something being lifted quickly.

examples.ko: 고기를 구울 때 불똥이 튀어서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Sparks flew while I was grilling meat, and I was startled.
Sparks flew up into the sky from the campfire.

examples.ko: 용접할 때는 불똥이 튀니까 보호 안경을 써야 해요.
examples.en: Sparks fly when welding, so you must wear protective glasses.

examples.ko: 촛불 심지에 불똥이 앉으면 불빛이 어두워져요.
examples.en: When a burnt bit forms on the candle wick, the light gets dimmer.

examples.ko: 팀장님 실수 때문에 우리한테까지 불똥이 튀었어요.
examples.en: Because of the team leader's mistake, we got dragged into it too.

examples.ko: 그 싸움의 불똥이 튈까 봐 멀리 피했어요.
examples.en: I stayed far away, afraid of getting caught up in that fight.

explain: '불꽃'이 타오르는 불의 모양이라면 '불똥'은 튀어 오르는 작은 불 조각이에요. 일상에서는 '불똥이 튀다'라는 비유로 특히 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 팀장님 실수 때문에 우리한테까지 불똥이 튀었어요.
phrases.en: Because of the team leader's mistake, we got dragged into it too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 한 일이 아닌데 다른 사람의 잘못이나 문제의 나쁜 영향이 나한테까지 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the bad effects of someone else's mistake or trouble reach you even though you did nothing.

explain_en: While '불꽃' is the shape of a burning flame, '불똥' is a small bit of fire that flies off. In daily life it is especially common in the figurative phrase '불똥이 튀다'.

examples.en: Flies are buzzing around the food.
A motorcycle roared out of the alley.
The machines at the construction site droned all day.
Honeybees fly around among the flowers, buzzing.

examples.ko: 선풍기가 붕붕대는 소리 때문에 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The humming of the fan woke me up.

examples.ko: 모기가 귀 옆에서 붕붕대서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: A mosquito buzzed next to my ear, and it made me angry.

explain: '붕붕거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. '-대다'는 소리나 행동이 계속 반복되는 느낌을 줘요. 벌레나 기계의 소리를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '붕붕거리다' and can be swapped with it. The '-대다' ending gives a feeling of a sound or action repeating again and again. Use it for the sounds of insects and machines.

examples.en: Suddenly a downpour poured down, and my umbrella was useless.
The game continued even in the pouring rain.

examples.ko: 밤새 내린 장대비 때문에 길이 물에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: The road was flooded because of the downpour that fell all night.
I ran home through the pouring rain.
When the downpour stopped, the sky cleared up.
They say it will pour heavily in the afternoon.

explain: 장대처럼 굵고 세차게 내리는 비를 말해요. '장대비가 쏟아지다/내리다'로 자주 쓰고, 뉴스의 '폭우'보다 구어적이에요. 잠깐 내리는 '소나기'와 달리 비의 굵기와 세기를 강조해요.
explain_en: It refers to rain that falls thick and hard, like poles. It is often used as '장대비가 쏟아지다/내리다' and is more colloquial than the news word '폭우'. Unlike a short '소나기', it stresses the thickness and strength of the rain.

examples.en: When it rains, the yard turns into mud.

examples.ko: 우리는 장화를 신고 진창길을 겨우 걸었어요.
examples.en: We wore rain boots and barely made our way along the muddy road.

examples.ko: 신발이 진창에 푹 빠져서 꺼내기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: My shoe sank deep into the mud and was hard to pull out.

examples.ko: 공사장 앞은 진창이라서 조심해서 가야 해요.
examples.en: It's muddy in front of the construction site, so you have to go carefully.
The rice-field path turned to mire because of the rain.

examples.ko: 차 바퀴가 진창 속에 빠져 움직이지 않았어요.
examples.en: The car's wheels were stuck in the mire and wouldn't move.

explain: 비가 온 뒤 질척질척해진 땅이나 길을 말해요. '진흙'은 흙 자체이고 '진창'은 그런 흙 때문에 질퍽해진 곳이에요. '진흙탕'이라고도 해요. '엉망진창'에도 들어 있지만, 혼자 쓰면 땅의 상태를 말해요.
explain_en: It means ground or a road that has become soggy and sticky after rain. '진흙' is the mud itself, while '진창' is the place made squelchy by it. People also say '진흙탕'. It appears inside '엉망진창' too, but on its own it describes the state of the ground.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 큰 폭발음이 들려서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by a loud explosion sound from the construction site.
When the fireworks began, booming sounds rang out one after another.
The baby burst into tears because of the loud bang.

examples.ko: 밤중에 폭발음 같은 소리가 나서 밖을 내다봤어요.
examples.en: I heard a sound like an explosion in the night and looked outside.

examples.ko: 영화 속 폭발음이 너무 커서 귀를 막았어요.
examples.en: The explosion sound in the movie was so loud that I covered my ears.
Residents who heard the blast evacuated quickly.

explain: '펑' 하는 소리를 설명하는 말이라서 뉴스, 사고 이야기, 영화 감상에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '펑 소리', '큰 소리'라고도 말해요. '폭발음이 들리다/울리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It describes a loud '펑' bang, so it comes up in news, accident stories and movie talk. In casual speech people also say '펑 소리' or '큰 소리'. It is used as '폭발음이 들리다' or '폭발음이 울리다'.

examples.en: Flames shot up from the building, so fire trucks were sent out.

examples.ko: 화염에 휩싸인 차에서 사람들이 겨우 빠져나왔어요.
examples.en: People barely escaped from the car engulfed in flames.
The whole mountain was covered in flames.

examples.ko: 소방관들이 화염 속으로 들어가 사람을 구했어요.
examples.en: Firefighters went into the blaze and rescued a person.
They say they came down the stairs to escape the flames.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 화염과 연기가 가득한 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a scene full of flames and smoke on the news.

explain: '불'보다 크고 거세게 타오르는 불길을 말할 때 써서 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '불'이나 '불길'이라고 해요. '화염에 휩싸이다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is used for big, fierce flames and shows up in news and writing. In everyday talk people simply say '불' or '불길'. A common pairing is '화염에 휩싸이다' (be engulfed in flames).

examples.en: When the wind blew, the dust rose up like a whirlwind.
A water whirl formed over the sea.
The fallen leaves spun around in a spiral shape.
A whirlwind blew and my umbrella flipped inside out.

examples.ko: 아이가 회오리에 휘말린 먼지를 신기하게 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The child watched in wonder at the dust caught in the whirl.
The whirl disappeared quickly, but everyone was startled.

explain: 바람이나 물이 빙빙 돌며 올라가는 모양이에요. 바람 이야기에서는 '회오리바람'이라고 자주 말하고, 물이나 마음속 혼란에는 '소용돌이'를 더 많이 써요. 큰 혼란을 비유할 때도 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 그 발표는 업계에 큰 회오리를 몰고 왔어요.
phrases.en: That announcement stirred up a huge upheaval in the industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 사회나 집단에 큰 혼란과 변화를 일으킬 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when something causes major turmoil and change in a society or group.

explain_en: It describes wind or water spinning around and rising. For wind people often say '회오리바람', and for water or emotional turmoil '소용돌이' is more common. It is also used figuratively for big upheaval.

examples.en: Last night a fierce blizzard raged all night.
A strong wind is sweeping across the seaside.
A typhoon is raging, so the ships can't sail.

examples.ko: 슬픔이 휘몰아치는 바람에 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Sorrow surged over me, so I couldn't say a word.

examples.ko: 소나기가 휘몰아칠 때는 밖에 나가지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't go outside when a downpour is sweeping in.
Suddenly a rainstorm started lashing outside the window.

explain: 바람, 눈, 비가 세게 한 방향으로 몰려올 때 써요. 감정이나 사건이 한꺼번에 밀려오는 느낌에도 쓰는데, 이때는 '슬픔이 휘몰아치다'처럼 주어가 감정이에요. '불다'보다 훨씬 거칠고 기세가 센 느낌이라 가벼운 바람에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: Use it when wind, snow or rain comes rushing in hard. It also describes emotions or events that surge in all at once, with the feeling as the subject, as in '슬픔이 휘몰아치다'. It sounds much rougher and more forceful than '불다', so it doesn't fit a gentle breeze.
